# Adaptive Workout Coach

Adaptive Workout Coach is a lightweight guided workout app: pure HTML, CSS,
and JavaScript, no build step, no server, no accounts. It runs as a static
site (GitHub Pages serves the docs/ folder). Open the URL and follow the
30-minute session, three times per week, even with no routine, no plan, and
no experience. Every exercise tells the user exactly what to do, in what
order, with big legible dose labels (sets x reps), muscle-group tags, and
demo video links where verified demos exist. No expertise required.

## The program

A 3-phase program, about 3 weeks per phase. The default week is Tuesday and
Thursday, and the user can choose other workout days. It is a workout
companion for someone returning after a long time off their feet, not a
personal prescription and not medical advice. It is provided as-is with no
warranty. Use it at your own risk and consult a clinician before starting.

Phase 1 "Stability & Tissue Tolerance" (14 exercises): low-load holds, glute
activation, balance, and a high-box sit-to-stand. Holds are a starting
point, not a treatment for pain. No deep loaded knee bending. The Spanish
squat hold stays around 30 to 45 degrees, and side-lying hip abduction
follows the clamshell. Phase 2 "Supported Unilateral" (13 exercises):
supported split squat, low step-up, kickstand-stance single-leg RDL, single-leg bridge, band
side-step, and a supported single-leg calf raise. Reduce support before
load, and do not add range and load in the same week. Phase 3 "Complex
Unilateral Loading" (15 exercises) is a placeholder until the full program
is confirmed. It includes a bodyweight Bulgarian split squat that starts at
3 x 6 each side, plus lateral step-downs, reverse lunges, and single-leg
calf raises. Week-3 dumbbells on the split squat are a placeholder too.
Sets, reps, holds, week doses, and the pain and swelling figures are
placeholder rules of thumb pending professional confirmation.

Moving up a phase uses Advance only, after 9 logged sessions and every
checklist item for that phase. Moving back is always allowed. Weeks are
minimums. Week 1, 2, and 3 doses sit inside each phase. Pain at or below
2/10 that settles to 2/10 or less within 24 hours is an acceptable rule of
thumb. Pain above that, or next-morning swelling, does not move the week
and, twice in a row, turns Advance off. Swelling advice says to cut volume
by about 30%. The app
never ticks the checklist from those scores and never rewrites the dose text.
No running or plyometrics until separately cleared.

## What the app does

- Runs a guided 30-minute workout with a single stored timer deadline, so
  closing and reopening the browser resumes with the correct time left.
- Full session lifecycle: start, pause, resume, clear (with confirmation),
  finish (pain check-in, then log), and timer expiry. Start does not wait
  on a clearance pop-up. A rest day is not logged.
- Per-exercise checklists, accordion sections, progress bar, sticky status
  bar, big dose labels.
- A Sun-Sat calendar. Workout days are chosen in the header settings panel
  and saved in this browser. The default is Tuesday and Thursday. The
  calendar, the selected day, rest days, and once-per-day logging follow
  that choice.
- "How it's organized" is in a header info panel, not in the main flow.
- A Demo videos section lists every exercise, and the same clip sits next
  to that exercise in the routine. Each exercise has one video_url. Players
  use the privacy-enhanced domain youtube-nocookie.com. Watch demo opens
  https://www.youtube.com/watch?v= for that clip. Only YouTube hosts are
  accepted as video ids. In-session
  library clips still come from docs/video-library.js through demo_ids.
  URLs are only added when verified, never invented.
- All progress is stored in the browser's localStorage under awc-demo-v1.
  No accounts, no analytics, no tracking, no personal data. Unreadable saves
  are backed up in the browser, the user is told, and only the latest few
  backups are kept.

## Project layout

- docs/index.html: app shell (status bar, timer, routine, calendar,
  phase picker, checklist, settings, info panel, demo videos). A
  Content-Security-Policy meta tag limits the page to its own files and
  allows demo frames from https://www.youtube-nocookie.com.
- docs/styles.css: styles, native CSS, light/dark aware.
- docs/app.js: all app logic: phases, timer, calendar, checklist,
  progression, symptoms. Progress persists in localStorage.
- docs/video-library.js: topic-organized demo video library. This is the
  file to edit when swapping videos.
- test/: node:test suites. Run with npm test. Not served from docs/.
- .github/workflows/test.yml: npm ci and npm test on pull requests.
- README.md: full documentation.
- FEATURES.md: feature list with status and location.
- llms.txt: this file.

## How to run it

Live: https://jhanisusM.github.io/adaptive-workout-coach/ (GitHub Pages,
deploys from docs/ on every push to main).

Locally: serve the docs/ folder with any static file server, e.g.
`cd docs && python3 -m http.server 8000`, then open http://localhost:8000.

Tests: `npm test` from the repository root.

## Safety

This is a workout companion, not medical advice. The app tells users to train
within a comfortable range, that sharp pain is a stop sign, and to follow
their clinician's guidance when training around an injury or condition.
A fixed footer line reads "Personal research project. Not medical advice; use
at your own risk." That line links to the README Disclaimer on GitHub. The
source is public on GitHub. All rights reserved.
